chunks: Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and his wife performed ghusl using five amdad from one vessel.”

Zurarah said to him, “How was it done?” He عليه السلام said: “He began and put his hand into the water before her, then cleansed his private part. Then she put hers in and cleansed her private part. Then he poured water, and she poured water over herself, until they finished. The amount with which the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله performed ghusl was three amdad, and that with which she performed ghusl was two mudd. It was only sufficient for both of them because they both shared in it together. But whoever performs ghusl alone by himself must have a saʿ.”

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: plural of mudd, a measured quantity of water
key_terms.إِنَاءٍ: a vessel or container used for water
key_terms.صَاعٍ: a saʿ, a larger standard measure of water
key_terms.فَرْجَهُ: his private part, washed in preparation for ghusl
key_terms.مُدَّيْنِ: two mudd, the amount used by the wife

ai.seo_question: How much water is sufficient for ghusl according to this hadith from Imam al-Baqir عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and his wife performed ghusl together from a single vessel using a measured amount of water. It explains the manner of their shared ghusl and indicates that sharing the water reduced the total amount needed, whereas a person performing ghusl alone requires a full saʿ.
